note: RI-DLG02: rumours MUST differ per town. RI-CHR02 §4c: '>= 2 race-specific rumours per settlement = 16'. Round 1 shipped 0 race-gated. A race-gated rumour is the same town gossiping differently at you: the square does not say the same sentence to a Saxhleel and to a Dunmer, and what it declines to say is the content.
w1_19_note: W1-19 round 2 added the main-quest rumours and the `adds_topics` field. Round 1 measurement: **0 rumour lines anywhere in game/data/dialogue/** named a main-quest noun**, and this file had no code consumer at all — it was loaded into `data.rumours` at engine.js and read by nothing after that. Under seam S8 there are no markers, so gossip is not decoration: it is the only thing that can tell a player who has just stepped off a barge what words to say to the Undersexton at Soulrest. A rumour carrying `adds_topics` puts those words into `sim.quest.topicsKnown` (see `game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js RumourBook`, read by `Conversation` via `Engine._installTopicSupply`), which is the only route into `Q-MAIN-01` that owes nothing to a prior quest. Existing rows are untouched; every addition is additive and the file is still declared incomplete for W1-11's own coverage.

thorn: The king pays in fish because he has nothing else, and he pays.
Something took the Ghen boy's boat and left the boy.

thorn.x: Soulrest has not read the Drowned Tally on time and the king's own dead are in it. He has said nothing about that in the hall and he has said a great deal about it in the yard.
The tree behind the hall has been saying the same four words since Second Seed and Sesh-Anaat has stopped writing them down.

stormhold: The Legion has not been paid since Sun's Height and the customs house knows it.
There is a milestone on the pass road that gives a distance to a place that cannot be found.

stormhold.x: There is a mortuary town down the coast that has missed a reading of the Drowned Tally for the first time in four hundred years, and the prefect has been sent three letters about it and answered none.
Eleven boxes came off an imperial bond at Archon and got to Soulrest weighing what an empty box weighs. That is a customs matter and the customs house would rather it were not.

soulrest.x: The Undersexton has been asking after a hand off the customs bench who can count and cannot be leaned on. Her name is Rell and she takes the reading room after noon.
Eleven boxes came up from the quay and went into the low chapel and a sexton has been on that door ever since.
The Ladder well has gone cold and the keeper has not left the rim. The carters will tell you so on the coast road and will not tell you so in here.

gideon.x: Soulrest is late with the Drowned Tally and the Wet Ledger has already worked out what that is worth. Ask the porter on the quay; he said it once and will not say it twice.
You cannot walk into the Archon bond store as yourself. Four houses in this town will lend you a name and every one of them wants a different thing back.
The market cross is where the coast road ends and the crypt road starts, and only one of those two is on a chart.

archon.x: The Court's reading is late and the Salt Factor has not stopped smiling about it since Second Seed. One of them down there is going to come and ask him for water.
The crane crew know what the sealed crates sound like when they land and will tell you for the price of a drink, provided nothing is written down.

blackrose.x: The yards send their dead down to Soulrest with the rest and the Drowned Tally has not been read this year, so no word has come back about where they are.
Neeja-Xul lost a blade out of the third yard in Rain's Hand and has not reported it, which is not like her at all.

helstrom.x: A Court letter came up the market stair asking after the root gallery, on account of the Drowned Tally not balancing, and Ashul-Tei has had it a month and not opened it.
Something in the gallery has been writing letters out for two hundred years and one of them arrived here.

lilmoth.x: Weeja-Sen has eleven names short on the hiring list every morning and they are the same eleven, and every one of them has a family sitting in the Drowned Tally waiting to be read.
The Company hires off the same wharf at a better rate and a worse contract and the wharf has started counting.

tidewrack.x: Everything that comes off a barge here is written down twice, and the second copy goes to Soulrest to be read against the Drowned Tally. It has not been read against anything since Second Seed.

race_gated.x: The king's fishermen found a net in the reeds with a House mark on the float and they buried it rather than report it.
They will smile at you in the square and count you out of the town at the gate. A tally gets kept.
The customs house has not sent a return to Cyrodiil in three quarters and the cohort has not mentioned it.
There is a room under the customs house with a lock on the outside and the cohort walks past it.
The factor house is taking on a new hand and the last one is not being talked about.
Wagons go out of the quiet street at the second bell and come back light, and the market has agreed not to hear them.
Two of the prison's gaolers are marsh-born and one of them has been letting letters out.
Half the men inside are in for things that are not crimes forty miles north of here.
The harbour master will not deal with the bands any more and the bands have stopped asking.
Something came up the harbour steps in the spring and the town has agreed it was a story.
The sapwell south of the town has gone quiet and the rootkeeper has stopped saying it has not.
They will take your coin at the gate and your questions at the wall, and the wall does not answer.
The tariff at Gideon is set by a man who has never seen a boat and it shows in the schedule.
They loaded a barge at Gideon at night and the manifest said reeds and reeds do not knock.
The Warden-Scribe was on the other side of that desk once and she says so about once a month, to one person.
What comes off a barge does not leave Tidewrack the same shape it arrived, and the Office writes the new shape down.
Egg-sibling, the Court has stopped saying the number out loud at the readings. Ask the undersexton what the number is and watch what her hands do.
They will not hire one of their own onto the Drowned Tally this year. That is why there is work here for a hand like yours and it is not a compliment.
The porter on the quay is one of ours and he has been down the crypt road this season, which is not done in this season. Ask him about the tally and let him decide.
The Factor will see a Dunmer. The Factor will not see a Dunmer who came down here on Court business and is pretending otherwise, so pick one before you knock.
The gallery will hear you out because of what you are. It will not agree with you because of what you are, and the keepers would rather you knew that at the top of the stair.
